See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Simple grade average = Sum of all percentage grades ÷ Number of grades

A worked example

For equally weighted grades of 80%, 90% and 85%, add the scores to get 255. Divide by 3 to get an 85% average. The lowest grade is 80% and the highest is 90%. A zero must be included if it is an awarded grade, not omitted as if it were blank.

Before you use the result

This tool accepts values from 0 to 100 and does not assign letter grades. An arithmetic mean is appropriate only when every entered grade has equal importance. For example, averaging 10/10 and 50/100 as percentages gives 75%, while pooling the points gives 60/110 = 54.55%. Neither method should replace your syllabus: choose the weighting system actually used for your course.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Should missing work count as zero?

Only if your instructor awards it a zero under the course policy. Work that has not yet been graded is different from a recorded zero.

Can I average letter grades?

This tool accepts percentages only. Use institution-defined grade points and credits in the GPA calculator for GPA-bearing courses.

What if one exam counts more than another?

Use the weighted grade calculator and enter the correct weight for each assessment.
